claims.text: Brittle behavior in an initially single-phase HEA emerges from chemical short-range order developing at or near grain boundaries under thermal and mechanical service conditions.
The proposed brittle behavior does not arise from conventional intermetallic precipitation or solute segregation.
Grain-boundary short-range order increases local heterogeneity in bonding strength.
The altered grain-boundary bonding impedes dislocation nucleation and promotes early crack initiation.
The initial material is a single-phase HEA with homogeneous elemental mixing, random atomic arrangements, and no detectable grain-boundary segregation or intermetallic phases.
Aging at 400–600°C under cyclic loading can stimulate diffusion and localized reordering without inducing bulk precipitation or full phase separation.
The structural mediator is microscopic short-range-ordered regions concentrated at or near grain boundaries without formation of a separate phase.
Grain-boundary short-range order can be detected using atom probe tomography or high-resolution TEM.
Thermal activation coupled with cyclic stress causes atomic rearrangements that produce short-range order at grain boundaries.
The resulting local order modifies interatomic bonding, hinders dislocation mobility, and promotes crack nucleation.
Thermally aged and cyclically loaded specimens will have lower fracture toughness and earlier crack initiation than the homogeneous baseline.
The treated specimens will exhibit increased grain-boundary short-range order without conventional grain-boundary segregation or intermetallic formation.
Conventional alloys degrade primarily through segregative embrittlement or precipitation.
The proposed mechanism applies to compositionally complex HEAs under elevated-temperature cyclic loading when overall phase stability is retained.
The mechanism may not operate when temperature and loading are insufficient to activate diffusion or when conditions trigger conventional precipitation.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as as-cast or rapidly solidified, whereas the comparison baseline is repeatedly described as as-annealed. These are materially different processing states, so the designated baseline is internally inconsistent.
